failures.finding: The fixture launches fluid_realtime_predict and then dereferences managed *count on the CPU to form later kernel arguments. The device reports concurrentManagedAccess=0. Normal execution crashes; unchanged binary with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 finishes all assertions. Forced synchronization is diagnostic only and does not qualify the fixture or performance.

Fails in the first PEG PAINT frame and in an isolated single-scene reproduction. CPU read of managed-address range fails with access denied. Forced kernel launch synchronization does not remove this failure. Production boundary code reads paint field metadata after asynchronous native clear operations; this is a source-level lead, not a symbolized root-cause proof.

The relocated public runner crashes at soft-body-fluid in --case all after 19 completed cases. Isolated normal-execution reproduction also fails with a managed-address CPU read and access-denied status. Exact runtime site requires follow-up diagnosis.

reference.relevance: NVIDIA documents that devices without concurrent managed access cannot access globally attached managed memory on the CPU while GPU operations make it inaccessible; Windows uses this restricted model. Device attributes and exception parameters are retained separately from the source-level diagnosis.
